purpose: Field-by-field classification of what a belief sample carries.

categories.PUBLIC_DETERMINED: complete legal public history determines it; grounds given
categories.RESAMPLED: drawn from a declared conditional law or a named approximation
categories.UNSUPPORTED: cannot be handled here; the branch refuses or is out of range

coverage_scan.role: COVERAGE STATISTIC ONLY. It never decides a category: absence of a counterexample is not an argument that public information determines a field, and it cannot detect a determined move whose hidden parameters are still unknown.

fields.visibility: the displayed attack damage, once an attack intent is shown
fields.grounds: The spawn range is public (Monster.cpp:118-120) and every attack intent the player is shown displays calculateDamageToPlayer(base), so the candidate set is narrowed by the displayed number and only ever shrinks. Sampling draws once from that set and keeps the draw; the true miscInfo is never read. Tests: tests/test_louse_hidden_base.py (fixed sampler agrees across two hidden values, pre-fix sampler diverges on the same pair).
fields.approximation: uniform prior over the spawn range, narrowed by public observations; not the original game's correlated posterior

fields.future_read: MonsterSpecific.cpp:774 (charges) and the charge state drives its move
fields.visibility: the charging intent is displayed on every turn it charges
fields.grounds: the counter only advances on turns whose intent the player sees, so counting them recovers it
fields.test: tests/test_native_coverage.py covers both of its moves

fields.init_write: set when Entangle is used, MonsterSpecific.cpp:1017
fields.visibility: Entangle applies Entangled to the player, so its use is public
fields.grounds: a boolean about whether a publicly visible debuff has already happened
fields.test: tests/test_native_coverage.py covers all three of its moves

fields.init_write: Monster.cpp:126-128, same pattern as the louse
fields.visibility: as the louse, but unreachable here
fields.grounds: Act 3 monster, not in the 17 supported encounters; the adapter refuses the encounter before this can arise, and widening the list requires applying the same candidate treatment
fields.test: the encounter whitelist rejects it (bridge.cpp supported_encounters)

fields.monster: THE_CHAMP, SPIKER, WRITHING_MASS, TIME_EATER, AWAKENED_ONE, BOOK_OF_STABBING, BRONZE_ORB
fields.field: miscInfo / monsterData read during move selection
fields.grounds: none of these is reachable in the 17 supported encounters; the read sites are recorded so widening the encounter list cannot forget them

fields.visibility: the intent class plus the displayed damage and hit count
fields.grounds: across 3584 reachable states and 93 distinct public signatures no two held moves shared a signature. The class alone does not separate Looter Mug from Lunge; the damage number does. The scan is the coverage evidence; the argument is that the adapter exports exactly those three fields and no more.

fields.future_read: the adapter, via the engine's execution events
fields.visibility: the move is watched resolving, and its class is exported
fields.grounds: taken from the engine's own execution events, not inferred from a turn counter

fields.field: aiRng, cardRandomRng, miscRng, monsterHpRng, potionRng, shuffleRng
fields.grounds: all six streams are reconstructed from the sampler seed
fields.approximation: independent streams, not the original game's correlated seeded streams

fields.init_write: shuffle at battle start and on reshuffle
fields.grounds: sorted by the cross-backend canonical key then shuffled with the sampler rng, so the sampled order never depends on the real one
fields.approximation: a uniformly random order over the public multiset

fields.grounds: zeroed in the copy; never an agent input
fields.approximation: no seed is modelled at all, which is strictly less information than the player has

fields.field: player state, card zones, powers, block, statuses

fields.init_write: MonsterGroup doMonsterTurn and the spawn sites (patch 0003)
fields.future_read: the adapter's previous_intent and slot reset
fields.visibility: only executed actions and spawns, both of which the player watches
fields.grounds: records only what actually happened; no rule reads it

RESAMPLED: all supported: aiRng, cardRandomRng, miscRng, monsterHpRng, potionRng, shuffleRng
PUBLIC_DETERMINED: all supported: moveHistory[1] and the executed history
all supported: player state, card zones, powers, block, statuses
all supported: the engine event log
UNSUPPORTED: THE_CHAMP, SPIKER, WRITHING_MASS, TIME_EATER, AWAKENED_ONE, BOOK_OF_STABBING, BRONZE_ORB: miscInfo / monsterData read during move selection

incomplete_evidence.item: miscInfo for monsters outside the 17 encounters
incomplete_evidence.why: read sites are recorded but no reachable path exists to test them

incomplete_evidence.item: post-execution identifiability of a move from its visible consequences
incomplete_evidence.why: assumed, not measured; the finer intent classes removed the need for it in the cases that were checked
sampled states, not a proof over all reachable states

explicitly_not_used_as_proof: the absence of a move_id key in the observation
